Location: Florida's Atlantic coast & Biscayne Bay – Fernandina Beach to Ocean Reef (NWS Jacksonville, Melbourne, Miami zones)
Item: UPDATE: Gale warning extended to midweek and stretched south to Ocean Reef and Biscayne Bay
Details: The northeaster is lasting longer and reaching farther south than yesterday's warning. NWS Jacksonville: Altamaha Sound GA to Flagler Beach out 20 nm, NE winds 25–35 kt, gusts up to 40 kt, seas 9–13 ft, until 2am EDT Tue Oct 27 (St. Augustine–Flagler 20–60 nm until 2am Wed). NWS Melbourne: Flagler Beach to Sebastian Inlet 0–20 nm, NE 20–25 kt, gusts to 35, seas 8–13 ft, until 2am Tue; Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 0–20 nm and all 20–60 nm waters, NE 25–30 kt, gusts to 35, seas 10–15 ft, until 2am Wed Oct 28. NWS Miami: Jupiter Inlet to Ocean Reef out 60 nm, frequent gale-force gusts from 8pm Sun Oct 25 to 8pm Tue Oct 27, seas peaking 12–15 ft Monday; Biscayne Bay also under a gale warning for the same hours. Why it matters: every Atlantic inlet from Fernandina to the upper Keys is dangerous for a sailboat through Tuesday, and now even Biscayne Bay will be a rough, gusty ride.
When: Sun Oct 25 – 2am EDT Wed Oct 28 2026 (end times vary by zone)
Notes: What to do: no outside passages or inlet runs before Wednesday; Miami/Biscayne Bay boats should be snugged in by Sunday evening — extra lines, chafe gear, check anchors. Small Craft Advisories are expected to replace the gale warnings midweek. Also: NWS Key West has a gale watch (not yet a warning) for the Straits of Florida and Gulf waters beyond 5 fathoms incl. the Dry Tortugas, early Mon to early Tue, NE 25–30 kt, gusts to 35, seas 7–11 ft. Map point is Biscayne Bay as a representative location. Follows yesterday's gale-warning row (Fernandina to Jupiter).

Location: Caloosahatchee River, Okeechobee Waterway – W.P. Franklin Lock (Alva) and Ortona Lock (LaBelle)
Item: Franklin and Ortona locks to close for major maintenance – Okeechobee Waterway shut to through traffic Jan 4 – Apr 30, 2027
Details: Notice to navigation: W.P. Franklin Lock closed to all traffic for dewatering and major maintenance Jan 4 – Mar 1, 2027, with Ortona Lock open to local traffic only; then Ortona closed to all traffic Mar 1 – Apr 30, 2027, with Franklin open to local traffic only. Why it matters: for about four months of peak snowbird season, boats can't cross Florida between Fort Myers and Stuart — sailboats headed coast to coast this winter need to go before Jan 4 or plan to go around via the Keys.
Notes: What to do: plan any cross-Florida transit before Jan 4, 2027, or route around via the Keys. Shift operators, 7am–5pm: W.P. Franklin Lock 863-662-9908; Ortona Lock 863-675-0616 or 863-662-9846. The notice doesn't define 'local traffic.' One forum post says the dates could stretch for weather or manatee protection — not confirmed by the Corps. Dates also reported by Waterway Guide (Oct 4) and WINK News. Related: the Point Chosen swing bridge on the same waterway is limited to 8 ft clearance through about Dec 22. Map point is Franklin Lock.

Location: The Rudder Club of Jacksonville, 8533 Malaga Ave, Jacksonville (St. Johns River)
Item: The Jimmy Buffett Race – a 20-mile river race and sandbar party
Details: The Rudder Club's race to remember Jimmy Buffett: about 20 nautical miles on the river, open to all boats — catamarans, dinghies, Flying Scots and cruisers — with a 'Cheeseburger in Paradise' raft-up and sandbar party north of the club dock from 2pm. Why it matters: one of the friendliest ways to join a race on the St. Johns — cruisers without a PHRF rating can get a provisional one.
Notes: What to do: register on Regatta Network; questions to Ken Kessler, 904-917-7245. Cruisers needing a provisional PHRF rating contact Rich Brew via the event page. The event page spells it 'Buffet,' and doesn't give the party's date — presumably race day. Race schedule is in a PDF on the event page.

Location: Sarasota Sailing Squadron, 1717 Ken Thompson Pkwy, City Island, Sarasota (Sarasota Bay)
Item: Penfield Memorial Flying Scot Regatta – Florida District regatta
Details: The Florida Flying Scot District regatta, sailed in memory of Jeff Penfield — the Penfield family's perpetual trophy goes each year to the sailor who does the most to grow the district and bring in new sailors. Why it matters: Flying Scots are the Gulf's classic family daysailer, and the Squadron on City Island by New Pass is an easy place to watch from shore.
Notes: What to do: Sarasota Sailing Squadron, 941-388-2355; registration on Regatta Network (Notice of Race posted Oct 5). Start times not on the event page. Same weekend as the Jubilee Regatta in Pensacola and the Multihull Rendezvous at Lakewood YC.

Location: Downtown Jacksonville – St. Johns River, Northbank and Southbank Riverwalks
Details: Decorated boats parade along both banks of the St. Johns River downtown, ending with fireworks; free to watch. Captains of motor-assisted vessels can enter, with a separate sailboat judging category (per the city's 2025 rules). Why it matters: a classic Thanksgiving-weekend sight from the Riverwalks — and the downtown docks fill up.
Notes: What to do: plan slips early if you want to watch from the water. The 6:30pm start comes from a community listing; the city's 2026 parade page and entry details weren't posted yet — check events.jacksonville.gov closer to the date.
